review.summary:
Phase 23 (AIRS management compatibility and security qualification) is substantive, well-architected work backed by real executed evidence rather than completion prose, but it lands below the 46/50 phase bar on accumulated minor defects, including one unaddressed medium evidence-integrity defect.

What I verified independently. The recorded gate docs/reviews/phase-23-attempt-01.checks.json contains exactly 71 records matching tools/check_phase.py's derived phase-23 plan, every one with exit_code 0, timeout false and source_unchanged true at source 7cfc104b…, and docs/checks/phase-23.json carries the same header with passed true; docs/checks/phase-23-partial.json shows the resumed prefix completed inside the eight-hour, source-and-plan-bound window. Rust evidence is real: 14 compiler/feature receipts exist for 1.89.0/1.99.0 (minimal, default, all, red-team, red-team-json-unification, json-unification, gateway, gateway-json-unification, default-tracing), and docs/checks/phase-23-rust-1.89.0-red-team.json records fmt --check, check/clippy --all-targets -D warnings, test --workspace and the red_team_management example run, with the 13 management contract tests, 3 derived-corpus tests and 6 overlay model tests all passing on MSRV. Both compilers ran the new source-matched clean package wrapper (docs/checks/phase-23-package-1.89.0.json and -1.99.0.json: schemaVersion 3, requireClean true, effectiveDirty false, releaseCommit cd6600c, sourceSha256 7cfc104b…, 148 no-default-feature and 208 all-feature lib tests, doctests, packaged example runs, external-crate consumer runs), and tools/red_team_management.py's final --verify-package-receipts gate re-verifies them after execution and fails closed for phases 24–25.

The runtime design matches the accepted plan. tools/red_team_management_models.py confines graph change to two enum vocabularies and two appended union tails, freezes the six baseline projection nodes and two union prefixes byte-for-byte, and rejects unreviewed vendor keywords, patterns, defaults, additionalProperties policies, divergent masked counterparts and renamed baseline models. Generated projections are correct in generated.rs:9313-9392 (representable value to Patch, lossless raw fallback into extensions, typed-over-raw on serialize, collision guard on baseline keys). The five target response declarations are derived, not asserted: tools/red_team_management.py:641-679 requires vendor required-field equality, full vendor-property coverage and nullable acceptance against the retained shared root, records explicit supersetJustification/comparisonLimit, and binds the operation matrix to a test name that red_team_management.py:730-733 proves exists. crates/scm-sdk/tests/red_team_management_contracts.rs asserts all five operations' methods, paths, operation names, both response modes, masked and credential-bearing branches, secret-free Debug/errors, exact per-page query-pair counts for list/pages/items/list_all, and no token acquisition or dispatch for five invalid profiling filters. Old-consumer compatibility is tested against real published bytes: tools/management_consumers.py pins the four 0.2.2 consumer sources to the verified registry archive c908cad8… and the phase-20 receipt and requires current repository bytes to equal them. The offline/live boundary holds (contracts/qualification.json liveReceipt null, liveVerified 0; live_evidence.py and check-access-release.py excluded with recorded reasons; CI runs only the 51-command contracts subset, enforced against docs/CI.md by tools/test_ci.py). No preserve_order feature is introduced (crates/scm-sdk/Cargo.toml:44).

Why it is not yet at the phase bar. One medium defect persists in current source: the synthesized external consumer crate declares no [features], so the frozen red_team_dataplane.rs consumer compiled only its empty cfg(not(feature="red-team")) fallback (receipt index 13: 0.25s, five unexpected-cfg warnings, empty stdout), while scripts/check-management-package.py accepts it as an "External consumer execution binding" with no disclosure; the underlying compatibility claim survives only through the in-archive --all-features example run. Alongside it, every low finding from the two accepted chunk reviews is still present at this same source hash (authored union-acceptance expectations undisclosed in the corpus evidenceBoundary, no final-report re-verification of checkpoint bindings, self-reported host identity in receipt verification, unreachable archive guard, unused import, nonconforming test formatting, doc comment after attributes), the phase and chunk scope declarations omit primary current-phase artifacts they govern, and the new derived-corpus test file has no test-name binding guard of the kind the contracts suite has.

findings.description: The synthesized external consumer crate (consumer/Cargo.toml copied from contracts/native-probes/Cargo.toml, which enables scm-sdk features but declares no [features] table of its own) makes cfg(feature = "...") in the copied consumer main.rs always false. The frozen published 0.2.2 consumer contracts/compatibility/management-old-consumers/0.2.2/red_team_dataplane.rs gates its entire body on #[cfg(feature = "red-team")] with an empty #[cfg(not(feature = "red-team"))] fn main() {} fallback, so the external consumer run at check index 13 in docs/checks/phase-23-package-1.89.0.json (line 996-1000: 0.278s, five 'unexpected cfg condition value: red-team' warnings, empty stdout) and in the 1.99.0 counterpart executed only the no-op fallback. scripts/check-management-package.py:100-111 nevertheless accepts that record as an 'External consumer execution binding', and the receipt's limitations array does not disclose it. One of four newly gated external consumer executions therefore proves only that the file parses as a crate root. The substantive old-consumer claim is still supported by the in-archive 'cargo run --example red_team_dataplane --all-features' at check index 6 (line 862-879), so this is an evidence-integrity overstatement rather than a missing acceptance criterion.
findings.required_fix: Add the features the frozen consumers gate on to the generated consumer manifest (for example '[features]\nred-team = []', or forward the scm-sdk feature set) so the cfg-selected body compiles and runs, and strengthen scripts/check-management-package.py to reject a vacuous run (require the expected stdout marker, or record per-consumer cfg selection). If vacuity is accepted instead, drop the 'external consumer execution' label for that consumer and state the limitation in the receipt limitations array and docs/CI.md.

findings.description: The phase-23 scope_evidence list, and the compatibility-matrix chunk list at line 5914, omit primary artifacts this phase actually produces or changes: crates/scm-sdk/src/models/red_team_management.rs (which now carries the generator-derived TARGET_PROFILING_FILTER_VALUES vocabulary emitted at tools/red_team_management_models.py:246), crates/scm-sdk/src/models/generated.rs, crates/scm-sdk/src/validation/schema_graph.json, contracts/red-team-management-union-extensions.json, crates/scm-sdk/tests/red_team_management_models.rs, crates/scm-sdk/examples/red_team_management.rs and NOTICE. All are hash-bound by in-scope ledgers (contracts/red-team-management-model-overlay.json sourceBindings; the vendor operations.json runtimeEvidence bindings) and regenerated under the executed generate_models.py --check, so the evidence exists, but PHASES.md:141-143 makes the declared scope the reviewer's map, and a reviewer following the declaration alone would not inspect the chunk's central runtime outputs. This repeats an unaddressed low finding from the accepted compatibility-matrix chunk review.
findings.required_fix: Add a new scope_revision for the compatibility-matrix chunk (preserving the attempt-1 revision) and extend the phase scope_evidence to list the generated model, graph, union-extension ledger, model/fixture test files and the management example, or record explicitly in the phase entry that these artifacts are covered by the enclosing phase review and bound through the overlay/runtime-evidence ledgers.

findings.description: The union acceptance booleans (requestAccepted/responseAccepted for the valid, missing-required, wrong-type, loose-format Vertex cases and the three multi-turn cases at lines 69-84) are hand-authored in the deriving tool, unlike the G25 corpus whose expected outcomes come from an independent Zod/AJV oracle. Inputs, required sets and pattern probes are genuinely vendor-derived, so the approach is reasonable, but the evidenceBoundary string describes the corpus only as 'Offline vendor-derived shape and independent preservation witnesses' and does not disclose that acceptance expectations are reviewed authored values. crates/scm-sdk/tests/red_team_management_fixtures.rs:94-109 asserts SDK behaviour equals those authored booleans, so the disclosure matters for how much independence the corpus establishes.
findings.required_fix: Extend the evidenceBoundary text or add an explicit expectationsOrigin field stating that union acceptance expectations are reviewed, vendor-schema-derived authored values rather than independent validator-oracle outputs; optionally cross-check them against an independent oracle as the G25 corpus does.

findings.description: The final phase report's 'passed' computation never re-verifies the per-record checkpoint_bindings against current bytes, and tools/review_phase.py:201-218 check_evidence does not either. read_checkpoint validates bindings only at resume start (line 776-778), and docs/checks is excluded from the source fingerprint (tools/review_phase.py:15), so a receipt bound by an earlier record in the same resumed session could be replaced by a later command in that session without invalidating the final report. Only the two package receipts are re-verified, by the final --verify-package-receipts gate. The recorded run was a resumed run (all 71 records carry checkpoint_bindings), so this is the live code path.
findings.required_fix: Recompute and compare checkpoint_bindings for every record when writing docs/checks/phase-N.json, and verify them again in review_phase.check_evidence before a receipt can qualify a review; add a test asserting that mutating an earlier record's bound receipt during a resumed session is detected before the final report is written as passing.

findings.description: verify_receipt validates schemaVersion, sourceSha256, toolchain, passed, requireClean, effectiveDirty, archive bytes, the complete member ledger, src/examples inventory equality, per-file byte equality and per-consumer execution indices, and requires each recorded cargo command to carry '+<toolchain>' and '--target <report hostTarget>' — but hostTarget and rustcVersion are taken from the receipt itself and never bound to the environment performing verification, unlike scripts/check-package.py:102-105 which resolves the real rustc host. A receipt produced on a different host, or with a mismatched recorded rustcVersion, still verifies.
findings.required_fix: Resolve the actual rustc host and version for the requested toolchain during --check and require report['hostTarget'] and report['rustcVersion'] to match, or record explicitly in the receipt limitations that host identity is self-reported.

findings.description: The guard rejecting archive member names starting with '.local/', 'contracts/', 'tools/' or 'node_modules/' is unreachable: line 44 has already restricted every accepted member to the explicit root_files set or the 'src/'/'examples/' prefixes. Only the suffix portion of the condition can still fire. Presenting an unreachable branch as a credential/development-input control overstates the published-archive policy when auditing it.
findings.required_fix: Either remove the unreachable prefix clause and keep the live suffix check, or reorder the two checks so the development/credential prefix guard is actually evaluated, and add a unit case exercising whichever guard is retained.

findings.description: verify_runtime_adoption binds all 13 contract test function names (MANAGEMENT_WIRE_TESTS, lines 615-629) into crates/scm-sdk/tests/red_team_management_contracts.rs, and tools/verify_native_fixtures.py has an equivalent --require-test-bindings gate, but the new derived-corpus suite crates/scm-sdk/tests/red_team_management_fixtures.rs has no such binding. tools/management_fixtures.py:92-97 records only that file's byte hash, which is regenerated whenever the file changes, so the three corpus tests (84 projection cases x 3 modes, union acceptance, enum additions) could be weakened or removed without any gate failing.
findings.required_fix: Add the three fixture test function names (all_twelve_projection_occurrences_preserve_independent_raw_oracles, vendor_union_required_types_formats_and_legacy_order_are_independent, all_vendor_enum_additions_and_unknown_response_values_roundtrip) to a bound test-name tuple checked the same way as MANAGEMENT_WIRE_TESTS, with a negative test proving removal fails.

findings.description: The plan (docs/red-team-management-0.86-plan.md:110-111) requires recording observable Unknown(JsonValue)-to-named-variant transitions. Both extended unions retain an Unknown(JsonValue) fallback, so payloads that previously decoded as Unknown now decode as Variant5(VertexAIConnectionParams) and Variant3(MultiTurnClientSessionConfig) — for example {"type":"client_session"}. The match-based fixture half of that requirement is met (red_team_management_fixtures.rs:115-135 and red_team_management_contracts.rs:77-82), and the release-notes half belongs to phase 24, but no source-bound artifact in this phase states the transition as a consumer-visible change, so phase 24 must re-derive it.
findings.required_fix: Record the transition in a source-bound artifact, for example a short field alongside runtimeUnionExtensions in the overlay ledger plus a sentence in the generated management addendum, naming both unions and the previously-Unknown shapes so the phase 24 changelog can cite rather than re-derive it.

findings.description: Code hygiene defects carried over unaddressed from the accepted chunk reviews at this same source hash: 'import copy' is unused in this module; tools/test_phase_checkpoint.py joins multiple statements with semicolons and omits spaces after call-argument commas (lines 22, 29, 34, 39-40, 44, 49-54, 59-65), departing sharply from the prevailing tools/ style such as this file; and crates/scm-sdk/src/models/red_team_management.rs:240-246 emits the reviewed VertexAIConnectionRedactParams doc comment after #[derive]/#[non_exhaustive], inconsistent with every other generated declaration.
findings.required_fix: Remove the unused import; reformat tools/test_phase_checkpoint.py to one statement per line with spaces after commas; and in tools/red_team_management_models.py's replace_once anchor target the attribute block so the doc comment precedes #[derive]/#[non_exhaustive].

evidence: docs/reviews/phase-23-attempt-01.checks.json:1-6 records phase 23, source_sha256 7cfc104b846782e27929eb5059e220716d47dd577498f3e7dc06c945f830b390, source_unchanged true, passed true; a count over the file shows exactly 71 "exit_code" entries and a regex search for "exit_code": [^0], "timeout": true and "source_unchanged": false returns no matches. The recorded command sequence matches tools/check_phase.py management_commands(23) (lines 189-285), including the 14 scripts/check-rust.py invocations, two scripts/check-native-exports.py, two scripts/check-management-package.py and the terminal red_team_management.py --check --require-through-phase 23 --verify-package-receipts.

Executed Rust evidence, not registered commands: docs/checks/phase-23-rust-1.89.0-red-team.json:1-150 shows passed true, sourceUnchanged true, rustc 1.89.0 host x86_64-unknown-linux-musl, cargo fmt --check, check and clippy --workspace --all-targets with -D warnings, cargo test --workspace (169 unit tests plus integration binaries: 13 red_team_management_contracts tests, 3 red_team_management_fixtures tests, 6 red_team_management_models tests, all ok), and 'cargo run --example red_team_management'. Both management suites are gated by #![cfg(feature = "red-team")] (red_team_management_contracts.rs:2, red_team_management_fixtures.rs:2), so the red-team sets are the ones that execute them. Fourteen distinct phase-23-rust-<compiler>-<features>.json receipts are referenced by the checks file.

Both compilers ran the source-matched clean package wrapper: docs/checks/phase-23-package-1.89.0.json:2-20 (schemaVersion 3, passed true, toolchain 1.89.0, requireClean true, effectiveDirty false, dirtyFieldPresent false, releaseCommit cd6600c53…, archive_sha256 3b32c829…) and :1039-1048 (sourceSha256 7cfc104b…, packageScriptSha256, wrapperSha256, oldConsumerManifestSha256 10cecd5e…, oldConsumerSources for all four published consumers); the 1.99.0 receipt matches with archive_sha256 c526b9da…. scripts/check-management-package.py:134-147 packages from a detached git worktree at HEAD and requires fingerprint(worktree) == fingerprint(ROOT) before and after, and :57-70 requires the archive's src/+examples inventory to equal the reviewed checkout's and every packaged src/examples/LICENSE/NOTICE/README/Cargo.toml.orig byte stream to equal current source.

Old-consumer compatibility uses real published bytes: contracts/compatibility/management-old-consumers.json pins response_defaults.rs, response_compatibility.rs and red_team_dataplane.rs to members of the verified 0.2.2 registry archive c908cad8b27863d0e2d3987f5554b196313877788ac8cfef35c16d589910db7c and native-probes/src/main.rs to the phase-20 receipt field publicConsumerSourceSha256; tools/management_consumers.py:62-84 requires current repository bytes to equal the frozen published bytes, rejects unowned/missing frozen files, symlinks and path escapes, and prints executionClaimed false. The in-archive runs at docs/checks/phase-23-package-1.89.0.json:843-937 execute response_defaults, red_team_dataplane, access_policies, response_compatibility and red_team_management with --all-features, each exit 0.

Overlay fail-closed design verified in source: tools/red_team_management_models.py:141-193 allowlists fragment vocabulary, string formats, the three reviewed Vertex patterns and the single client_session default, and rejects unreviewed records/additionalProperties policies; :65-95 independently rediscovers the six projection nodes in the frozen graph and requires exact vendor component/field coverage plus identical masked counterparts; :197-216 requires the six projection nodes and both union/enum nodes to equal the frozen baseline byte-for-byte, asserts the legacy union branch count before appending exactly one tail, and :267-283 verifies the emitted tail against the reviewed ledger before the strict baseline comparison.

Five response declarations are derived, not asserted: tools/red_team_management.py:641-679 resolves the retained root from crates/scm-sdk/src/validation/schema_graph.json, requires the vendor response $ref per operation, requires SDK required fields to equal vendor required fields and every vendor property to exist, rejects any declared-nullable field the SDK would reject, and emits per-operation supersetJustification, comparisonLimit, responseModes and a fixture binding; contracts/vendor/red-team-management/0.86.0/compatibility-decisions.json:4788, :5509, :6252, :6854, :7602 carry those five rows, and the cited test name is enforced to exist by red_team_management.py:730-733 via MANAGEMENT_WIRE_TESTS (:615-629).

Request/response, secrets, omission/null and pagination behaviour asserted at the wire: crates/scm-sdk/tests/red_team_management_contracts.rs:345-459 drives 5 providers x 4 auth shapes x 2 response modes through get/create/update/probe/update_profile and asserts operation names, methods, exact paths, raw byte equality in ResponseWithoutDefaults, validator-normalized equality in Response, and absence of the synthetic secret in Debug; :165-180 proves ResponseWithoutDefaults round-trips bytes while Response injects ws_response_timeout 110 and basic_auth_location HEADER and keeps explicit null basic_password; :466-538 asserts the profiling filter and legacy status appear on every page of list/pages/items/list_all with exact query-pair counts; :540-558 asserts zero token acquisitions and zero dispatches for five invalid filter values; :561-569 asserts malformed responses never echo credentials.

Typed projection semantics verified in generated code: crates/scm-sdk/src/models/generated.rs:9313-9352 decodes basic_username/basic_password into Patch and re-inserts the raw value into extensions on decode failure, and :9354-9392 serializes typed values first, guards baseline-key collisions and skips colliding extension keys; crates/scm-sdk/tests/red_team_management_fixtures.rs:57-88 exercises all 84 vendor-derived cases in three modes with typedPresence and secret-free Debug assertions, and contracts.rs:572-602 proves collision override and unset restore.

Offline/live and CI boundaries hold: contracts/qualification.json:34-41 has liveReceipt null with liveVerified 0 / liveRecorded 0, tools/red_team_management.py:740-755 rejects any current live receipt or inherited live annotation, tools/check_phase.py:263-268 excludes check-access-release.py, check-package.py and live_evidence.py from phase 23 with explicit reasons, and tools/test_management_phases.py:147-150, :192-205 assert live_evidence is absent at 23 but present at 24, the final receipt gate is the last command and follows both package commands, and neither it nor the wrapper appears in the CI subset. tools/test_ci.py:131-146 binds docs/CI.md's documented 71 full and 51 CI command counts to len(commands_for(23)) and len(ci_commands_for(23)); .forgejo/workflows/ci.yml:73 runs --phase 23 --verification-only --contracts-only.

Regression breadth actually executed: the checks file records 'unittest discover -p test_*.py' at 457 tests OK (line 596) plus focused suites test_red_team_management 44, test_review_phase 51, test_management_phases 25, test_management_package 14, test_management_consumers 7, test_management_fixtures 4, test_g25*.py 31, test_ci 36 and others, all OK; generate_models.py --check and --verify-fixtures (27479 typed cases), management_fixtures.py --check, management_consumers.py --check, g25_report.py --check, native-exports on both toolchains with 3820 frozen capabilities, and a fresh dependency audit (docs/checks/phase-23-dependencies.json: passed true, lockfileUnchanged true, 206 locked packages, vulnerabilities.found false) are all present at exit 0. crates/scm-sdk/Cargo.toml:44 enables only serde_json feature "raw_value" — no preserve_order.
limitations: Read-only review with Read/Glob/Grep only: I executed no commands and could not recompute SHA256 values, so the declared reviewed-source hash 7cfc104b… and checks hash 4207c87d… are taken as given. I verified internal consistency (per-record exit codes, source_unchanged flags, receipt sourceSha256/cargoLockSha256/consumer hashes, checkpoint completeness, command-plan equality against the derived list) rather than cryptographic authenticity.
No check was re-executed. Pass/fail conclusions rest on the recorded invocations, exit codes, stdout/stderr and the source-binding logic in the verifying scripts.

I could not run git, so attribution of which files changed in phase 23 versus phase 22 is inferred from the phase-status review_findings_disposition, the phase-22 scope list and generator ownership (for example the generator-emitted TARGET_PROFILING_FILTER_VALUES). The scope-completeness finding rests on that inference, not on a diff.

The retained clean archives live at untracked absolute paths under .local/package-worktrees/cd6600c…/.local/artifacts/; I did not read those bytes, so archive_sha256 3b32c829… and c526b9da… are supported only by the receipts' member ledgers and the per-file source-equality checks in scripts/check-management-package.py. The docs/checks receipts referenced by the checks file are untracked and therefore outside the reviewed source hash; they are bound by the recorded checkpoint_bindings and by the final package-receipt gate.

Generated model correctness was assessed through the compiler receipts, selected generated declarations (the two extended enums and their schema-bound counterparts, the three new structs, both union enums, BasicAuthAuthConfig/RestConnectionParams projections) and the independent fixture/check evidence, not by reading the full generated.rs.

I did not re-derive the vendor OpenAPI content independently; pin verification (mp-openapi.yaml 5fbb533b…, normalized openapi.json equality) is taken from the tools' own guards, which the recorded tamper tests exercise.

I read no credential or tenant-registration file and inspected nothing outside this repository. Nothing here establishes live service acceptance; fresh tenant qualification, changelog migration guidance, release version selection, publication and terminal remote CI are phase 24 deliverables and were not judged. CHANGELOG.md correctly carries no management 0.86 entry yet.

Cumulative inherited infrastructure (G25 corpora, gateway specimens, Portkey, data-plane ledgers) was treated as passing inputs through their executed checks rather than re-audited, per the scoped-change instruction.
